clue.text: French actress turning to a whore

indicators.note: turning tells us the whole run of letters is read backwards, end to start

parts.note: taken as written
a drab is an old word for a slattern or prostitute

explanation.surface: A French film star is said to be taking up prostitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses TO + DRAB as one run to give the actress's surname; Brigitte Bardot is the famous French film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigitte Bardot was a celebrated French film star of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: For instance, I'm at heart echoing Verne primarily?

definitions.text: For instance, I'm at heart echoing Verne primarily?

parts.note: 'as' introduces an example, just like 'for instance'
I'm written without its apostrophe

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letter of the word echoing
primarily points to the opening letter of the name Verne

explanation.surface: A writer wonders whether, deep down, he is simply an imitation of Jules Verne.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: Isaac Asimov was a science-fiction writer who might be thought to echo Jules Verne, the genre's pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov, like Jules Verne, wrote science fiction, so he could be seen as following that pioneer.

clue.text: Juan, say, who's come over from a land East of Eden

indicators.note: come over suggests turning the word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Genesis says Cain went to dwell in the land of Nod, east of Eden

explanation.surface: Don Juan is pictured as a wanderer arriving from the biblical land where Cain was exiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Juan as an example: Don Juan, the legendary seducer, has the Spanish title Don.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is a Spanish title of respect for a gentleman, as in Don Juan.

clue.text: Author of Aminta's soliloquies

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken from within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A question about who wrote the speeches in the pastoral play Aminta.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'Aminta's soliloquies'; Torquato Tasso, the Italian Renaissance poet, really did write the pastoral drama Aminta.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was an Italian poet and playwright, a writer of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: In which we see Queen avoids lunatic and 17 plays one

indicators.note: lunatic suggests the letters of avoids have gone mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film is described where a deranged queen tries to keep away and an actor takes a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 17-across is Peter Ustinov, who played Nero in the 1951 film; 'In which we see' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The epic film about Nero's Rome is one in which Ustinov took a starring role as the emperor.

clue.text: Volumes depicting Queen of the South briefly, including acceptable pictures

indicators.note: including means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: QOS is the short form of Queen of the South, a Scottish football club
U means socially acceptable, upper-class usage
art is paintings and pictures

explanation.surface: Books illustrated with a portrait of a southern queen and some decent images.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen of the South is a Scottish football club from Dumfries, abbreviated QOS; U for 'acceptable' comes from the U and non-U distinction of upper-class English.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book size, so these are books or tomes.

clue.text: What Kellerman called part of the school year for alumni?

indicators.note: for here places the alumni's piece first, the term given over to them

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
a session is a term or period of the academic year

explanation.surface: A thriller writer seems to name a school term set aside for former pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Kellerman, the American crime novelist, wrote a novel with this title; 'for' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Kellerman gave this title, meaning a fixation, to one of his Alex Delaware crime novels.

clue.text: Ret Marut mostly sitting in broken chairs with mouldings

indicators.note: sitting in places one piece inside the other
broken means the letters of chairs are smashed up and rearranged
mostly means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Ret Marut was one of the pseudonyms of the novelist B. Traven

explanation.surface: A mysterious author is found perched among smashed chairs, with plasterwork.
explanation.walkthrough: B. Traven was the elusive author of The Treasure of the Sierra Madre; 'broken' turns chairs into ARCHIS, which takes the shortened pen name inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An architrave is the moulded frame around a door or window.

clue.text: Lacking which, Bourne found himself all at sea

definitions.text: Lacking which, Bourne found himself all at sea

parts.words: Lacking which, Bourne found himself all at sea
parts.note: Jason Bourne, found floating in the sea with amnesia, does not know who he is, as in Ludlum's first Bourne novel title

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Ludlum's amnesiac spy has lost his sense of self, the thing a name and memory supply.

clue.text: Daisy's worried about one at drunken orgies

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes around the other letters
worried suggests the letters of Daisy are agitated and rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter
I is the Roman numeral one
on can mean at, as in being on or at a place

explanation.surface: A girl called Daisy is anxious about someone at wild parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns the girl's name into DYSIA; 'at' as ON is the sense of being on or at a place. 'Daisy's' carries an apostrophe s that adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dionysia were Athenian festivals of Dionysus, god of wine, with revelry and drinking.

clue.text: Like Unsworth's hunger for a measure of land in a US state

indicators.note: in places the measure of land inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the abbreviation for South Dakota
an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: Someone hungry for a patch of ground in America, like a character in an Unsworth novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry Unsworth's Booker-winning novel about the slave trade is titled 'Sacred Hunger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsworth's novel title pairs hunger with this adjective, meaning holy or revered.

clue.text: Courtesan involving ex- Chancellor in sole mix-up

indicators.note: involving means the anagram wraps around the politician
mix-up means the letters of sole are jumbled

parts.note: Norman Lamont was a British Chancellor of the Exchequer in the early 1990s

explanation.surface: A scandal in which a famous mistress is entangled with a former finance minister over a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix-up' turns the fish into LOES; Lola Montez (the clue's film spelling, from Max Ophuls's 1955 film) was a dancer and royal mistress. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish dancer became the mistress of King Ludwig I of Bavaria, a famous nineteenth-century kept woman.

clue.text: Where Keith Talent may have taken aim quickly?

definitions.text: Where Keith Talent may have taken aim
definitions.meaning: Keith Talent, the darts-mad lout in Martin Amis's London Fields, would aim for the outer ring that doubles a score
a military phrase meaning at a run, fast

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at running pace, and is also the outer scoring ring on a dartboard.

clue.text: Fragment at start of Iliad

definitions.meaning: the Greek title of the epic, Ilias, begins with the Greek letter I

explanation.definitionFit: The smallest Greek letter gives the idiom for a jot, a tiny scrap.

clue.text: Go abroad and produce foreign-language edition with grim version for learner

indicators.note: for means one set of letters stands in place of another

parts.note: to translate is to put a text into another language
L is the learner sign on British cars
a version of grim is its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Instructions to travel and bring out a translated book, gloomily adapted for a student.
explanation.walkthrough: In TRANSLATE the L is replaced by MIGR, letters of 'grim' rearranged; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmigrate is to move from one country or place to another, to migrate.

clue.text: A Sartre play seen behind closed doors?

parts.note: Huis Clos is Sartre's play, known in English as No Exit

explanation.surface: A Sartre play staged in private.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means in camera, behind closed doors; the question mark admits that the definition is in English but the answer French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French legal phrase means in private, with the public excluded.

clue.text: Robert — historically English enthralled by leader

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the following piece

parts.note: dux is Latin for leader
ever can mean at any time in the past

explanation.surface: A Robert from history who was held spellbound by a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was the favourite of Elizabeth I, so 'historically English' and 'enthralled by leader' also suit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert, second Earl of Essex, bore this family name.

clue.text: Event I arranged with Proust as raconteur

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A literary event organised around Proust, featuring a storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of EVENT I and PROUST are rearranged together; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor and writer was famous for his witty storytelling and impressions on chat shows.

clue.text: Greek hero — Procrustes' bottom half he destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are wrecked and rearranged
in a down clue the bottom half is the final half of the name

explanation.surface: A Greek hero defeated a bandit, cutting him in two.
explanation.walkthrough: The last half of PROCRUSTES is USTES; with HE it is rearranged. Fittingly, this hero killed Procrustes in the myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian hero who slew the Minotaur and the robber Procrustes.

clue.text: 17's autobiographical expression of self-worth

definitions.meaning: Peter Ustinov's memoir bears this title
read literally, the phrase calls oneself precious, as well as being a mild exclamation

explanation.definitionFit: Ustinov's memoir title doubles as a mild exclamation and, literally, as calling oneself beloved.

clue.text: One seen in Palatine Rome

indicators.note: in signals that the answer lies within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone spotted on one of the hills of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor sits inside 'Palatine Rome', where he built his palace; the grid's HERO looks like a misprint, as the clue gives only the emperor's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor whose palaces were on and around the Palatine Hill.

clue.text: Clorinda or Tisbe, nasty pest to resist violently

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of pest are rearranged
violently shakes up the letters of resist

explanation.surface: Two operatic characters are urged to fight off an unpleasant nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Clorinda and Tisbe are Cinderella's two half-sisters in Rossini's opera La Cenerentola; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Each is a daughter of Cinderella's stepmother, so related to the heroine by marriage.

clue.text: Hill, say, one found at the foot of South America

indicators.note: found at the foot of means the last piece goes at the bottom, after the others

parts.note: US is the United States
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A hill pictured as lying at the southern tip of the American continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Hill as an example: Susan Hill is the English author of The Woman in Black.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Hill is an English novelist, so she is an example of a woman with this name.

clue.text: Lady's song only half finished — Mrs Grieve's was modern

parts.note: her means belonging to a lady

indicators.note: only half finished means the word loses its second half

parts.note: a ballad is a song

explanation.surface: A woman's song is left incomplete, while another woman's work was up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: Maud Grieve wrote the 1931 reference book 'A Modern Herbal' on medicinal plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Grieve's famous book is a guide to plants and their medicinal uses, the kind of book named by the answer.

clue.text: Where you'll see son rile uncle at last in confusion?

definitions.text: Where you'll see son rile uncle at last in confusion?

indicators.note: in confusion means the letters are muddled into a new order
at last points to the final letter of the word uncle

explanation.surface: Where a son angers his uncle in a chaotic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' rearranges SON RILE to ELSINOR. The whole clue also describes Hamlet, set at the Danish castle where Hamlet torments his uncle Claudius.
explanation.definitionFit: The castle at Helsingør in Denmark is the setting of Shakespeare's Hamlet.

clue.text: Pinch, at home, backing Pecksniff initially

indicators.note: backing means the preceding piece runs backwards

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of Pecksniff

explanation.surface: Dickens's hypocrite Pecksniff is shown stealing something at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Pecksniff is the hypocrite in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit, whose put-upon assistant is Tom Pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip is to squeeze sharply between finger and thumb.

clue.text: "Comment is free but facts are on -" (Tom Stoppard)

definitions.text: "Comment is free but facts are on -" (Tom Stoppard)

parts.words: "Comment is free but facts are on -" (Tom Stoppard)
parts.note: a journalist's quip in Stoppard's play Night and Day, mocking reporters charging their outlay to the paper

explanation.definitionFit: Journalists claim costs back from their papers, so facts come at the employer's charge.

clue.text: Where Ferrante's plans went awry about end of June?

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes around the final letter
went awry means the letters of plans are rearranged
end of points to the last letter of June

explanation.surface: Somebody's plans went wrong around late June.
explanation.walkthrough: Elena Ferrante's Neapolitan Quartet is set in this Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrante's four novels about two friends are set in the southern Italian port.
